title: Vasilisa the Beautiful
subtitle: A Russian folk tale
source: after the collection of Alexander Afanasyev
documentTitle: Vasilisa the Beautiful — an interactive 3D fairy tale
description: The Russian folk tale “Vasilisa the Beautiful” in 3D: scroll through the chapters as riders gallop through the night forest, skulls glow on the fence and Baba Yaga flies to her hut on chicken legs. With narration and music by Mussorgsky.

ui.narrateTitle: Read aloud with the browser’s voice

prologue.title: Prologue
paragraphs: In a certain kingdom there lived a merchant, and he had an only daughter — Vasilisa the Beautiful. Dying, her mother blessed her with a little doll and told her to keep it safe and show it to no one.
The merchant married a widow with two daughters. The stepmother and her daughters disliked Vasilisa and kept thinking how to be rid of her.

fire.title: The Fire Goes Out
paragraphs: One autumn night every light in the house went out. “Go to Baba Yaga for fire!” cried the sisters, and they pushed Vasilisa out of the door.
Vasilisa fed her doll, hid it in her pocket and set off into the dark, dense forest.

white-rider.title: The White Rider
paragraphs: She walks and she trembles. Suddenly a rider gallops past: he is white, dressed in white, his horse is white and its harness white — and the dawn began to break.

red-rider.title: The Red Rider
paragraphs: She walks on — another rider gallops by: he is red, dressed in red, on a red horse.

sunrise.title: Sunrise
paragraphs: And the sun rose. Warm rays broke through the spruce branches and lit up Vasilisa’s face.

clearing.title: The Clearing
paragraphs: All day long Vasilisa walked, and only toward evening did she come to the clearing where Baba Yaga’s hut stood. The fence around it was made of human bones, and on the fence were skulls with eyes.

black-rider.title: The Black Rider
paragraphs: Then a rider came again: he was black, dressed all in black, on a black horse. He galloped up to the gate and vanished as if the earth had swallowed him — and night fell. The eyes of the skulls on the fence began to glow.

baba-yaga.title: Baba Yaga
paragraphs: Soon a terrible noise rose in the forest: trees creaked, dry leaves crackled. Out of the forest came Baba Yaga — riding in a mortar, driving it with a pestle, sweeping her tracks with a broom.

tasks.title: The Tasks
paragraphs: Baba Yaga gave Vasilisa a whole day’s work. But the doll helped: while Vasilisa slept, everything was done.

skull.title: The Skull Lantern
paragraphs: Baba Yaga let Vasilisa go and gave her a skull with burning eyes set on a stick. Vasilisa ran home, and the skull lit her way.

epilogue.title: Epilogue
paragraphs: By the evening of the next day Vasilisa reached home. And the hut on chicken legs remained standing in the dense forest.
